title: Keep parenthetical information unambiguous
text: Use parentheses for a clear reference, item identifier, step marker, introduced abbreviation, or brief supplementary explanation when they help the reader. Keep required actions, prerequisites, limits, and branch-selection criteria explicit in the main instruction, not only in parentheses. Expand a parenthetical alternative into explicit choices with their selection criteria. Choose a singular or plural form, or a quantifier that states the intended quantity, instead of attaching a parenthetical plural ending. Avoid dense or nested parenthetical prose; use separate sentences or a structured list when relationships become difficult to follow.
exceptions: Do not infer that every noun has a regular plural or that either number is interchangeable. Preserve the intended cardinality, agreement, and established term; obtain clarification when the quantity is unknown.

Preserve parentheses and other delimiters exactly in marked commands, code, schema expressions, interface strings, quotations, and other syntax-controlled text. Their syntactic role is not a prose choice.

A brief explanation may remain parenthetical only if it is supplemental; necessary conditions and limits must remain visible in the main flow. Do not omit them to simplify a sentence. Escalate conflicting external requirements to the responsible editor or technical owner.
Examples do not approve a vocabulary or executable syntax. Supporting target IDs are planning references only, not canonical relation endpoints or delegated source facets.

segments.text: If the service uses the primary region, open the primary-region log. If the service uses the recovery region, open the recovery-region log.

allowed.rationale: Each alternative has an explicit condition and matching action. Neither the region choice nor its condition is hidden in parentheses.

segments.text: . The parentheses belong to the expression, not to a prose aside.

allowed.rationale: The syntax-controlled fragment retains its exact delimiters. The example demonstrates preservation, not validation of a complete expression for a particular engine.

segments.text: Open the primary-region (recovery-region) log (depending on the service region).

not_allowed.rationale: The compact alternative and parenthetical condition hide branch selection. State each condition and action explicitly as in the positive example.

segments.text: Context: the procedure requires exactly one selected log. Instruction: Open the log(s).

not_allowed.rationale: The parenthetical plural suggests an unsupported choice of quantity. Write Open the selected log. Do not automatically expand every compact form into a plural instruction.

facets.source_facet: Parentheses can supply references, item identifiers, procedure markers, abbreviations, and explanations.
facets.rationale: Retain these useful functions in IT prose when the information is clear and supplemental, while excluding required constraints from asides.

facets.source_facet: The source permits compact singular-and-plural forms and parenthetical alternatives.
facets.rationale: Require explicit cardinality and branch selection instead of ambiguous compressed choices; do not presume regular noun plurals.

facets.source_facet: Source explanations can place operational limits inside parentheses.
facets.rationale: IT readers and independently retrieved instructions need required limits in the main procedural flow, not merely in an aside.

criteria: Review all uses allocated from ASD-STE100 Issue 9 rule 8.3, physical PDF pages 109-110, including explanations, limits, number, and alternatives.
Verify cardinality and branch criteria with the technical context. Check that supplemental references remain possible and that no noun-plural assumption or executable delimiter rewrite is introduced.

Check original English wording, examples and literal digest, applicability, exceptions, separate source rights, attribution, and planned dependencies. A structural pass does not establish semantic completeness or editorial approval.
